candidates.title: Police recover $54K in Hot Wheels after BNSF freight train burglary in California
candidates.excerpt: Police recovered approximately $54,000 in stolen Hot Wheels merchandise following a freight train burglary in Colton, California. A witness called 911 around 3 a.m. Thursday, October 22, reporting suspicious activity near railroad tracks. Officers spotted a black Chevrolet Silverado leaving the area and initiated a traffic stop. The investigation ended with one arrest and 350 boxes of toy cars in police custody. According to video released by the Colton Police Department, the caller reported people stealing merchandise near Maple Street. An officer positioned himself near Seventh Street and La Cadena Drive while monitoring the surrounding roads. Footage shows authorities following the pickup before stopping its driver. The man exited with his hands on his head, and officers took him into custody. The department confirmed the recovery in its October 22 Facebook announcement. candidates.title: Container freight rates diverge as global benchmarks rise and Asian indexes weaken
candidates.excerpt: Global container freight rates delivered a mixed performance in the latest weekly assessments, with major international benchmarks moving higher while Chinese freight indexes showed more subdued results. The divergence was particularly evident on Asia-Europe routes, where Drewry reported further increases but the NYSHEX Freight Index (NYFI) continued to decline. Drewry’s World Container Index (WCI) rose 2% to US$4,585 per 40-foot container, reaching its highest level in 15 weeks. The Freightos Baltic Index (FBX) also advanced, increasing 5% to US$3,560. Meanwhile, the China Containerized Freight Index (CCFI) declined, while the Shanghai Containerized Freight Index (SCFI) and Ningbo Containerized Freight Index (NCFI) registered marginal gains. The latest figures highlight an uneven freight market, with movements varying considerably across benchmarks and individual trade lanes. candidates.title: Maersk updates fuel fees in Australia and New Zealand
candidates.excerpt: Maersk has announced new Intermodal Fuel Fee levels for landside transportation services in Australia and New Zealand. The revised monthly rates will apply from 1 November 2026. Australia fuel fee reduced Maersk will apply a 25% Intermodal Fuel Fee across five Australian states. The new rate represents a reduction from the 27% fee applied during October. New Zealand fee remains unchanged In New Zealand, Maersk will maintain the Intermodal Fuel Fee at 27% from 1 November. The carrier introduced the fee on 16 March 2026. It appears as EFS for exports and IFS for imports. Maersk attributed the measure to pressure from global energy prices and fuel availability. The carrier also pointed to the evolving security situation in the Middle East and its effect on landside and intermodal transportation costs. The surcharge levels will be reviewed monthly. Maersk said further adjustments may be required as energy market conditions develop.

candidates.title: Hambantota Port sees new opportunities as container ships return to Suez
candidates.excerpt: Hambantota International Port Group (HIPG) expects a sustained return of container shipping through the Red Sea and Suez Canal to create new commercial opportunities for the Sri Lankan port, as it prepares to expand its container handling capabilities. The port operator believes that the restoration of the established East–West shipping corridor could strengthen Hambantota’s position in regional transshipment networks, while supporting demand for bunkering, ship supplies and other marine services. The outlook follows an October 2026 assessment by maritime consultancy Linerlytica, which forecasts a full-scale return of container shipping to the Suez route by the first quarter of 2027. However, the pace of any recovery remains dependent on security conditions and individual shipping lines’ operational decisions. Located approximately ten nautical miles from the main East–West shipping route, Hambantota is seeking to capitalise on its geographical position as carriers reconsider diversion

candidates.title: Jade Pacific makes liner debut with Red Sea service
candidates.excerpt: A new Singapore-based container shipping company headed by former SeaLead executives has entered the liner trades with a service connecting India, Pakistan and Egypt’s Red Sea coast. Jade Pacific Line (JPL), established in April this year, has deployed the 1,100 teu Medkon Sia on a rotation linking Mundra, Nhava Sheva, Karachi and Sokhna before returning to Mundra. According to liner consultancy Linerlytica, the service commenced on September 25 and operates on an irregular 30- to 35-day rolling schedule rather than a fixed weekly frequency. The operation provides a direct connection between two of India’s largest container gateways, Pakistan’s principal port and Egypt’s Sokhna, which serves the Suez Canal corridor and the Egyptian hinterland. JPL is affiliated with Chinese-linked container operators Ocean Silk Line (OSL) and OVP Shipping, with OSL holding a 30% stake in the newly established company.

candidates.title: Nuclear ships only pay off under the IMO’s net-zero rules, UCL study finds
candidates.excerpt: Nuclear ships only pay off under the IMO’s net-zero rules, UCL study finds Nuclear propulsion can compete in container shipping only if an effective global emissions policy is in place and reactor costs fall sharply, according to new research from the UCL Energy Institute’s Shipping and Oceans Research Group. It is one of the most detailed total cost-of-ownership assessments of nuclear merchant shipping to date. The report, Nuclear Reactors for Merchant Shipping: A Total Cost of Ownership Assessment of a Low-Carbon Pathway, compares a large container ship (14,500 to 19,999 TEU) with nuclear propulsion against conventional fuel oil and dual-fuel ammonia vessels. It uses a literature review, interviews with five UK-based experts in law, insurance, classification, technology development and industry representation, and a cost model run with and without the IMO Net-Zero Framework (NZF). candidates.title: SMART-TD’s Soo Line members ratify agreement with CPKC
candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — Members of the International Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail, and Transportation Workers-Transportation Division who work on the former Soo Line have ratified a three-year agreement with CPKC, the union announced last week. The agreement, effective through Dec. 31, 2027, includes “significant” increases in hourly wages, SMART-TD said. Pay increases are retroactive to 2025, with new increases taking effect Jan. 1, 2027. In balloting concluded on Oct. 15, 75.6% of those taking part voted in favor of the agreement, with 24.4% against. Some 81% of eligible voters cast ballots. “Of all the numbers associated with this agreement, the one I’m most proud of is the 81% voter participation,” General Chairperson Vince Ramirez said on the SMART website. “To me, that speaks volumes about our membership. It tells me our members are paying attention, they’re engaged, and they care about the decisions that affect their livelihoods.” — To report news or errors, contact trainsnewswire

candidates.title: Midwest Overland Rail Preservation Society acquires last operable SD9043AC
candidates.excerpt: PERRY, Okla. — The Midwest Overland Rail Preservation Society has acquired Union Pacific No. 3568, the last intact and operable EMD SD9043AC diesel from the railroad’s original fleet of 309 units, the organization announced. The locomotive joins the society’s collection, which includes the prized Milwaukee Road Bicentennial SD40-2 No. 156 and UP DDA40X Centennial No. 6925. No. 3568 was built in April 1997 for UP, originally as No. 8138. It was changed to its current number on June 1, 2015. The SD9043ACs hold distinction as the world’s largest single-unit diesel locomotive ever built. “Aside from units that were remanufactured into SD70ACUs by Progress Rail, the SD90 model is on the verge of extinction, with No. 3568 currently being the only known operable example,” said society President Jordan Biggs. “We plan to keep No. 3568 in operable condition for future excursion use, and it will eventually be restored to its factory number of No. 8138.” — To report news or errors, contact trains

candidates.title: CSX expands Chambersburg, Pa., intermodal terminal
candidates.excerpt: CHAMBERSBURG, Pa. — Reflecting growing freight volume, CSX has made moves to increase capacity at its Chambersburg Intermodal Terminal. The railroad said last week that it has added a rubber-tired gantry crane and two reach stackers, along with additional parking for containers, chassis, and employees. Expansion of the terminal’s maintenance facility is also under way, and the railroad is evaluating further additions. Volume at the terminal, approximately 55 miles southwest of Harrisburg and 85 miles northwest of Baltimore, has increased from approximately 159,000 units in 2023 to about 192,000 in 2025 — a nearly 21% increase. “These investments help us work smarter, but it’s the people who make the difference,” Terminal Manager Tracy Brasfield said in a CSX news release. “Our team’s focus on safety, communication and execution allows us to keep pace with growth and provide reliable service to customers.” The 85-acre Chambersburg facility was opened in September 2007 at a cost of $46 m

The orderbook-to-fleet ratio has consequently risen to 26%, well above its historical average of 14%, pointing to a substantial expansion in carrying capacity over the coming years. candidates.excerpt: Chief Financial Officer Jennifer Hamann will retire in early 2027, Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP) has announced. Hamann, who joined Union Pacific in 1992, was named CFO in January 2020. She had previously held leadership roles in a broad range of areas, including finance, human resources, marketing and sales, investor relations, and corporate audit. “For 35 years, she led with integrity and heart, guiding our finances through historic challenges, executing our strategy, mentoring future leaders and representing Union Pacific across the industry,” UP Chief Executive Jim Vena said in release. “Jennifer was tough — she never said yes unless she believed it was the right thing to do for Union Pacific. She made this railroad stronger, and her contributions will be felt for generations. I am deeply grateful for her leadership and friendship.” Hamann is the first woman to serve as the railroad’s chief financial officer.
